JPM.rationale: JPM presents a strong fundamental-valuation disconnect: Q1 2026 EPS grew 17.2% YoY to $5.94, operating margin expanded to 41.1%, and ROE improved to 16.2%, yet the P/E has compressed from ~16.3-16.7x in late 2025 to 14.36x — the market is paying materially less for higher-quality earnings. The franchise is dominant (#1 in deposits, credit cards, global IB fees for 17 consecutive years, $7.1T in client assets) and Q1 results confirm execution (EPS beat by $0.44, revenue +10% YoY, CIB revenue +19% YoY, IB fees +28% YoY). Near-term catalysts include the SpaceX IPO mandate (largest in history, ~$75B raise), Q2 IB fee guidance of +10%+, and the stress test buffer freeze freeing capital for $40B+ in buybacks. The score is capped below +0.5 by: (1) expense guidance raised to ~$106B (+$1B), (2) flattening 10Y-2Y spread to 0.42% as a modest NII headwind, (3) $13B projected G-SIB surcharge threatening ROE, and (4) $50B private credit exposure amid sector stress. The revenue discrepancy between the quant pack ($49.84B) and qual news sources ($50.54B) is noted but not material to direction; I rely on the quant pack's $49.84B as the primary reported figure.
